policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'that he will bring home thy seed' renders a transitive causative with 'thy seed' as its object, which is the hiphil yashiv of the qere; the ketiv ישוב reads as the qal 'return', intransitive, which the ASV's transitive 'bring home ... And gather' does not render.
ASV 'And stretcheth her wings toward the south' has the plural 'wings', matching the plural suffix of the qere כנפיו; the ketiv כנפו is the singular 'his wing', which the ASV plural does not render.

ASV 'Her young ones also suck up blood' has the plural 'young ones' with a plural verb, matching the plural suffix of the qere ואפרחיו; the ketiv ואפרחו is the singular 'his young one', which the ASV plural does not render.
